text:
Starting by checking what build123d offers for building a channel from a centerline (`trace`, `JernArc`), which is the cleanest way to make a constant-width 2D duct.

```python
import subprocess
for pat in ["trace", "JernArc", "Polygon", "def offset", "export_step", "scale"]:
    r = subprocess.run(["grep","-n",pat,".reference/b123d_api.md"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    print("###",pat); print(r.stdout[:1200])
```
I'll run the reference search through the tool.

`trace` and `JernArc` exist, so I can build the duct from its centreline at constant 6 mm width. First test the arc sign convention and the loop centreline geometry numerically, before making any faces.

Now build the fluid region in mm: main channel centreline traced at 6 mm, plus four loop centrelines (straight leg out at 135°, 195° clockwise arc R=7, return leg at −60° back to the channel axis). Plot before believing anything.
One face, 120 mm long. Now look at it: sample the face's wires and draw them.

The topology is right: two openings per unit — the 135° branch (easy-direction flow cannot turn into it) and the −60° return leg, with a teardrop island between them. Now scale to metres once and export the planar face.
The width print above was a hard-coded number, not a measurement. Measuring it properly from the geometry instead — arc radii in the loops, and a probe across the plain channel.
Measured 6.00 mm both in the straight channel and across the loop annulus. Now the coarse mesh: quad-mesh the face in gmsh, extrude one cell in z, classify the extruded side faces.
gmsh imported the STEP as mm (its default target unit), so the model is 1000× too big. Redo with `OCCTargetUnit=M` and verify the bbox is 0.12 m before meshing.
Classify every boundary surface by its own bbox — the inlet/outlet are the only planar faces at x=0 and x=0.12 by construction — then mesh coarse.
Classification caught nothing — gmsh's bboxes must carry a tolerance pad. Inspect the actual numbers.
Pad is 1e-7; use tol 1e-6, rebuild the physical groups and rewrite.
Mesh written with named patches. Now a minimal OpenFOAM case and `gmshToFoam`.
Patch names didn't come through. Check what's actually in the .msh.
Physical tags in the elements (7–12) don't match the names block (1–6) after my `removePhysicalGroups`. Rebuild the whole gmsh stage cleanly in one self-contained cell with explicit tags.
Names are right. Now set the 2D types: `front`/`back` → `empty`, `walls` → `wall`, then `checkMesh`.
Mesh OK at 1835 cells. Draw the quad layer to see the cells resolve the loops.
The picture came back but the cell used a name from an errored cell; re-emit it self-contained.

Shape confirmed: straight through-path plus four teardrop islands, return legs meeting the channel at 60° pointing upstream. Now refine to 0.5 mm (12 cells across the channel) and redo the OpenFOAM conversion.
Mesh OK at 6426 cells. Final measurements straight off the geometry and the mesh: junction angles, patch areas, thickness.
The 135° stub walls are only ~3 mm long and got filtered out; re-measure with a lower threshold.
Exporting per-patch STLs of the same solid so the surface checks have the geometry to compare against (the mesh itself came from gmsh, not snappy).
Built and meshed. Declaring complete.
